newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on fund-induced sag.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on fund-induced sag.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures ended lower in line with a fund-selling sag that pressured all U.S. wheat markets, although traders said commercial buying helped limit the kind of losses seen in KCBT and CBOT wheat.
"We had big, commercial-type buying in here," a trader said. "It took Chicago to melt down for us to tick down."

Traders in Kansas City said the fund selling was brought on when CBOT November soybeans failed to effectively break resistance at $8.00 per bushel. Chicago traders also said wheat was pressured by ideas that overall world wheat production will be higher than earlier estimates.
MGE spring wheat closed three to eight cents per bushel lower, with Sept down 4-1/2 cents at $4.64 per bushel. Dec lost 7-3/4 cents to end at $4.58.
Traders said Benson Quinn bought 1.5 million Dec bushels and Country Hedging bought one million Dec. Atwood/Peavey reportedly bought one million Sept and sold 1.3 million Dec.
MGE barley futures closed unchanged to 27 cents per hundredweight lower, with Sept unchanged at $7.60. Dec lost nine cents to close at $7.52.
The MGE estimated Wednesday's spring wheat volume at 23.772 million bushels, versus 33.107 million Tuesday.
